description: A team studio in which students deliver a real software product for a client over a full lifecycle, from scoping and architecture spikes to sprints, deployment, quality gates, user testing and handover. In the lab they work through client, team and incident scenarios, draw architecture and plans, run pipelines and cloud deployments, and defend their choices at reviews.
modelledOn: Bass, Clements and Kazman, Software Architecture in Practice
Schwaber and Sutherland, The Scrum Guide
outcomes: Elicit and scope a client's needs into a prioritised backlog with acceptance criteria and a justified minimum viable product.
Make and document architectural decisions, using spikes and design reviews to retire the highest risks early.
Plan and deliver work in sprints, managing estimates, dependencies, change requests and team conflict.
Build a continuous integration and deployment pipeline and operate the service with monitoring and incident response.
Apply code review, automated testing and quality gates, and manage technical debt.
Run usability and acceptance testing with real users and hand over a maintainable product with a candid retrospective.

units.title: Studio set-up, client brief and scoping
topics: The studio model: team formation, roles, working agreements and cadence
Eliciting needs from a client: interviews, personas, user stories and domain modelling
Scoping a minimum viable product: MoSCoW, impact mapping and explicit non-goals
Estimation under uncertainty: relative sizing, ranges and re-estimation
Statement of work, acceptance criteria and managing client expectations

units.title: Architecture spikes and design review
topics: Architectural drivers: quality attribute scenarios and lightweight trade-off analysis
Spikes and prototypes to retire technical risk
Documenting architecture: the C4 model, UML views and architecture decision records
Build versus buy, API design and data modelling; offline-first design for low-connectivity users
Running a design review: preparation, roles and recording outcomes

units.title: Sprint planning and delivery
topics: Scrum events, backlog refinement and definitions of ready and done
Kanban flow: work-in-progress limits, cycle time and bottlenecks
Trunk-based development, short-lived branches and feature flags
Tracking delivery: velocity, burndown and cumulative flow without gaming the numbers
Working with the client: demos, feedback loops and change requests
Team dynamics: conflict, pairing, mob programming and fair contribution

units.title: Build, deploy and operate
topics: Continuous integration pipelines: build, test, lint and artefacts
Containers and infrastructure as code
Deployment strategies: blue-green, canary, rollback and database migrations
Observability: logs, metrics, traces and service level objectives
Incident response, on-call practice and blameless post-mortems
Hosting choices for African users: latency, data residency, cost and power or connectivity failures

units.title: Code review and quality gates
topics: Code review practice: small changes, checklists and constructive feedback
The testing pyramid: unit, integration and end-to-end tests, and meaningful coverage
Static analysis, dependency scanning and secure-coding gates in the pipeline
Technical debt: measuring it, recording it and paying it down
A team definition of done and automated quality gates

units.title: User testing and acceptance
topics: Usability testing: task design, think-aloud sessions and the system usability scale
Accessibility, localisation (Twi, Ewe, Hausa and French) and low-bandwidth design
Acceptance testing: behaviour-driven scenarios and user acceptance sessions
Performance and load testing against service level objectives
Security review and privacy impact assessment under data-protection law
Release readiness review and go/no-go decision

units.title: Handover and retrospective
topics: Handover package: documentation, runbooks, architecture overview and client training
Licensing, ownership of code and contribution to open source
Retrospective formats, individual contribution evidence and peer assessment
Final client demonstration and presentation
Support, maintenance planning and the cost of ownership after release

schedule.title: Forming the studio team and meeting the client
schedule.exercise: Agree team roles and working rules, then interview a role-played client (a Kumasi spare-parts wholesaler) and turn the notes into five personas-based user stories with acceptance criteria.

tasks.title: Choose roles and working agreements for a five-person team in a scenario and handle an early disagreement, scored on the rubric
Interview a client scenario, pick questions that uncover the real problem and record which needs were found and which were missed
Model the client's domain as a class or entity diagram and write 8 user stories each traced to an element of the model

schedule.title: Scope, estimates and the agreement
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page scope: MVP features ranked by MoSCoW, non-goals, an estimate range per feature and acceptance criteria the client signs.

tasks.title: Draw an impact map linking a client goal to actors, impacts and deliverables, and mark which deliverables belong in the first release
Estimate ten backlog items with relative sizes in a scenario, then update the forecast after a surprise and explain the change to the client
Negotiate a statement of work in a scenario where the client wants twice the scope in the same time, scored on honesty and trade-offs

schedule.title: Architectural drivers and spikes
schedule.exercise: List the three most important quality attributes for the client's product, write a scenario for each and design one spike that tests the riskiest technical assumption.

tasks.title: Rank quality attributes for a clinic booking app in a scenario and write measurable quality scenarios for the top three
Draw C4 context and container diagrams for the studio project and record two architecture decisions with the alternatives rejected
Run a spike that measures whether a chosen library handles 1000 records on a low-end phone profile and report the result against the target

schedule.title: Design choices and design review
schedule.exercise: Decide build versus buy for authentication and payments (mobile money API), choose offline behaviour for patchy connectivity and defend the architecture at a mock review.

tasks.title: Draw a sequence diagram of an offline-first sync between a phone and a server, including conflict handling and retries
Compare managed and self-hosted database options on a cloud console for the project's load and cost and record the choice
Face a design review scenario with a hostile reviewer, answer five questions with evidence and score on clarity and honest treatment of risk

schedule.title: Sprint planning and flow
schedule.exercise: Plan the first sprint from the backlog with a sprint goal, a definition of done and capacity, and compare a Scrum board with a Kanban board using work-in-progress limits.

tasks.title: Build a sprint plan with goal, selected stories, capacity per person and a visible definition of done on a task board diagram
Run a Kanban scenario with a bottleneck in testing, apply a work-in-progress limit and observe the effect on cycle time
Practise trunk-based development in a repository using short branches, a feature flag and a merge, and keep the main branch always releasable

schedule.title: Delivery metrics, clients and team health
schedule.exercise: Run a sprint review and retrospective for a role-played sprint, handle a mid-sprint change request, and address an uneven contribution in the team.

tasks.title: Draw a burndown chart from sprint data with a late scope addition and explain what it does and does not show
Handle a client change request mid-sprint in a scenario, weighing impact, the sprint goal and the agreement, and score the response
Resolve a team conflict scenario involving a dominant member and a silent member using fair-contribution practices, scored on the rubric

schedule.title: Continuous integration and containers
schedule.exercise: Set up a pipeline that builds, tests and lints on every push, packages the service in a container, and deploys to staging with a rollback.

tasks.title: Write a pipeline script that runs build, unit tests and lint on a sample project and fails when any step fails
Write a container file for a small web service, build the image, run it and check the health endpoint from the terminal
Deploy a service to two instances behind a load balancer using blue-green, switch traffic and roll back after an injected failure

schedule.title: Observability and incidents
schedule.exercise: Define two service level objectives for the product, add metrics and alerts, and run a game-day incident where the database becomes slow, ending in a blameless post-mortem.

tasks.title: Create dashboard metrics and an alarm for error rate and latency on a deployed service and trigger the alarm with failure injection
Lead an incident-response scenario with a slow database, follow the evidence to the cause and write the timeline and fixes
Estimate monthly hosting cost for the product in two regions with different latencies to Accra and choose with a stated trade-off

schedule.title: Reviews, tests and quality gates
schedule.exercise: Review a teammate's pull request with a checklist, raise the test coverage meaningfully (not just numerically) on one module, and add a quality gate that blocks a failing merge.

tasks.title: Review a pull request scenario with five planted problems, write comments and score on defects found and the tone used
Add unit and integration tests to a module so that a planted bug fails a test, then fix the bug and show the suite passes
Run a dependency scan and a static analysis check on a repository, triage the findings and gate the pipeline on severity

schedule.title: Usability testing and accessibility
schedule.exercise: Test the prototype with five real users on three tasks, collect think-aloud notes and a SUS score, and write acceptance scenarios in given-when-then form for the top stories.

tasks.title: Run a usability session scenario, observe task failures, compute a system usability scale score and list the top three fixes
Test a screen on a small low-end phone profile with a slow connection and text in two languages, and fix truncation and large images
Write behaviour-driven scenarios for the checkout story and automate them against a sample app so they pass or fail with the feature

schedule.title: Performance, security and release readiness
schedule.exercise: Load test the service against its objectives, complete a privacy impact assessment for the data collected, and run a go/no-go meeting with evidence.

tasks.title: Load test a service with a rising request rate on the cloud console, find the saturation point and apply autoscaling to meet the target
Run a privacy impact assessment scenario for a customer-data app under the data protection act and choose controls for each risk
Decide go or no-go in a release-readiness meeting scenario with open defects, weighing the evidence and scored on the rubric

schedule.title: Handover and licensing
schedule.exercise: Assemble the handover package (README, architecture overview, runbook, training outline), choose a licence for the code and complete peer-assessment forms with evidence from the repository.

tasks.title: Produce an architecture overview and a runbook page for the deployed system that a new engineer could use to restart it safely
Choose a licence and ownership terms for the delivered code in a client scenario and justify against the client's goals
Use the repository history to compile each member's contribution evidence by commits, reviews and tickets, and note the limits of such data

schedule.title: Final demonstration and cost of ownership
schedule.exercise: Give the final client demonstration with a live deployment and a fallback, present a support and maintenance plan with costs, and submit an honest retrospective.

tasks.title: Prepare a live deployment for the demonstration with a health check and a scripted fallback to a recorded run if the service fails
Draw a support plan with response tiers, a maintenance schedule and a three-year cost of ownership table for the client
Present to a client panel scenario, answer hard questions on risks and cost, and be scored on clarity, evidence and candour
